blogTitle: How Long Does Gallery Wall Installation Take?
videoTitle: How Long Does Gallery Wall Installation Take?
script:
How Long Does Gallery Wall Installation Take?

[warmly] Okay — so you've been dreaming of a gallery wall… but every time you think about actually DOING it, you just… put it off, right?

Here's the thing — a typical 8 to 12 frame arrangement takes between THREE and SIX hours start to finish, and once you break it into phases, it's honestly so much less daunting.

There are FIVE phases — planning and layout design, gathering your tools, preparing and marking the wall, hanging the frames, then final levelling and styling… each one takes its own slice of time, you know?

[sighs] I helped a client once who was convinced her 10-frame living room gallery would take about an hour… we spent 45 minutes on Phase THREE alone, just measuring and marking.

Wall TYPE, frame COUNT, layout complexity, and the tools you've got — these four things will either save you hours or cost you them, so it's worth knowing BEFORE you start.

A small 5-frame gallery wall? That's roughly ONE to two hours for a confident DIYer… but scale up to 15 frames and you're genuinely looking at a full day.

And every extra frame you add? Add roughly 8 to 15 minutes of active hanging time each — it really does stack up, trust me.

Now, the wall MATERIAL makes a real difference — drywall is fastest, but lath-and-plaster or solid masonry can add 20 to 40 minutes per session, easily.

Think of it this way — drywall is your easiest scenario, Victorian plaster needs a little more patience, and brick? That's a proper commitment with the right DRILL bit.

The ROOM also matters a lot — a staircase gallery wall is genuinely one of the most time-consuming spots in the house, while a hallway or living room wall is much more straightforward.

[curious] You know why staircases take longest? You're working at changing heights, often on a slope — it's fiddly in a way a flat living room wall just isn't.

DIY versus professional installation — a pro can do in TWO hours what takes a first-timer five or six, but honestly, the DIY process is where most people find the satisfaction.

Before you touch the wall — PLAN your layout on the floor or use paper templates taped up first… this one step alone can save you an hour of re-hanging.

Paper templates on the floor, painter's tape on the wall, or a digital planning app — each method saves time differently, and picking the right one for your layout MATTERS.

[warmly] The BIGGEST time-wasters? Not pre-measuring frames, skipping a spirit level, and starting without all your hardware to hand — these three things alone can cost you two hours.

A little tip I love: always complete your planning and tool-gathering the day BEFORE you hang — arriving at the wall with everything sorted is a total game-changer.

To SPEED things up — use a laser level instead of a traditional spirit level, batch-hang frames of the same size together, and mark every hook position before you pick up the hammer.

These small tweaks genuinely keep your alignment SHARP without adding any extra time — it's the difference between a gallery wall that looks effortless and one that looks… slightly off.

Here's your planning checklist — layout design, tools gathered, wall prepped, frames marked, then hung and levelled… and each task has a realistic time next to it so you can plan your day PROPERLY.

[excited] Task by task — 30 to 60 minutes planning, 20 to 30 gathering tools, 30 to 60 on the wall prep, 45 to 120 hanging, and 20 to 40 for final styling… that's your WHOLE day mapped.

Now for a bit of INSPIRATION — layouts that work in any home… a symmetrical grid is the most time-efficient, while a salon-style mix of sizes is the most dramatic.

A grid of IDENTICALLY-sized frames on flat drywall is honestly the easiest scenario — it's the layout I'd always suggest to anyone doing their first gallery wall.

And mixed-media arrangements — photos, prints, maybe a small mirror or shelf — those are STUNNING but do factor in extra time for the planning phase, you know?

Creating a gallery wall that LASTS means using the right fixings for your wall type, keeping a note of hook positions, and leaving a small gap for future additions… it's a living thing, honestly.

So before you start — think about your wall material, how many frames you're hanging, and have your layout SORTED the day before… and you'll honestly wonder why you kept putting it off.

Did you know styling your home doesn't have to be guesswork?

We've built a free set of Home Decor tools and styling guides…

From colour theory and design principles to gallery wall layouts and art sizing. Download them all from our site!

Find all you need to transform your home into a calming oasis!

Happy Decorating!
